groups.name: U.S. Civics
groups.attribution: Questions and answers from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), 2008 civics test. U.S. government work, public domain. Officeholder names can change — confirm at uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates.

decks.name: American Democracy
decks.description: Constitution, rights, and the rule of law (questions 1–12).

cards.front: What is the supreme law of the land?
What does the Constitution do?
cards.hint: Also accepted: defines the government; protects basic rights of Americans

cards.front: The idea of self-government is in the first three words of the Constitution. What are these words?
What is an amendment?
cards.hint: Also accepted: an addition (to the Constitution)

cards.front: What do we call the first ten amendments to the Constitution?
What is one right or freedom from the First Amendment?
cards.hint: Also accepted: religion; assembly; press; petition the government

cards.front: How many amendments does the Constitution have?
What did the Declaration of Independence do?
cards.hint: Also accepted: declared our independence; said the United States is free (from Great Britain)

cards.front: What are two rights in the Declaration of Independence?
cards.hint: Also accepted with pursuit of happiness

cards.front: What is freedom of religion?
cards.back: You can practice any religion, or not practice a religion.

cards.front: What is the economic system in the United States?
cards.hint: Also accepted: market economy

cards.front: What is the “rule of law”?
cards.hint: Also accepted: leaders / government must obey the law; no one is above the law

cards.front: Name one branch or part of the government.
cards.hint: Also accepted: legislative; President; executive; the courts; judicial

cards.front: What stops one branch of government from becoming too powerful?
cards.hint: Also accepted: separation of powers

cards.front: Who is in charge of the executive branch?
Who makes federal laws?
cards.hint: Also accepted: Senate and House of Representatives; the national legislature

cards.front: What are the two parts of the U.S. Congress?
cards.back: the Senate and House of Representatives

cards.front: How many U.S. Senators are there?
We elect a U.S. Senator for how many years?
Who is one of your state’s U.S. Senators now?
cards.hint: D.C. and territories have no U.S. Senators

cards.front: The House of Representatives has how many voting members?
We elect a U.S. Representative for how many years?
Name your U.S. Representative.
Who does a U.S. Senator represent?
Why do some states have more Representatives than other states?
cards.hint: Also accepted: they have more people

cards.front: We elect a President for how many years?
In what month do we vote for President?
What is the name of the President of the United States now?
cards.hint: Confirm at uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates

cards.front: What is the name of the Vice President of the United States now?
cards.hint: Confirm at uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates

cards.front: If the President can no longer serve, who becomes President?
If both the President and the Vice President can no longer serve, who becomes President?
Who is the Commander in Chief of the military?
Who signs bills to become laws?
Who vetoes bills?
What does the President’s Cabinet do?
What are two Cabinet-level positions?
cards.back: Secretary of State and Secretary of Defense
cards.hint: Many Cabinet titles are accepted, including Attorney General and Vice President

decks.name: Courts and Federalism
decks.description: The judiciary, federal vs state powers, and parties (questions 37–47).

cards.front: What does the judicial branch do?
cards.hint: Also accepted: explains laws; resolves disputes; decides if a law goes against the Constitution

cards.front: What is the highest court in the United States?
How many justices are on the Supreme Court?
cards.hint: Confirm at uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates

cards.front: Who is the Chief Justice of the United States now?
cards.hint: Confirm at uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates

cards.front: What is one power of the federal government?
cards.hint: Also accepted: declare war; create an army; make treaties

cards.front: What is one power of the states?
cards.hint: Also accepted: police; fire departments; driver’s licenses; zoning

cards.front: Who is the Governor of your state now?
cards.hint: D.C. does not have a governor

cards.front: What is the capital of your state?
What are the two major political parties in the United States?
What is the political party of the President now?
cards.hint: Confirm at uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates

cards.front: What is the name of the Speaker of the House of Representatives now?
cards.hint: Confirm at uscis.gov/citizenship/testupdates

cards.front: Describe one amendment about who can vote.
cards.back: Citizens eighteen (18) and older can vote
cards.hint: Also accepted: no poll tax; any citizen can vote; a male citizen of any race can vote

cards.front: What is one responsibility that is only for United States citizens?
cards.hint: Also accepted: vote in a federal election

cards.front: Name one right only for United States citizens.
cards.hint: Also accepted: run for federal office

cards.front: What are two rights of everyone living in the United States?
cards.back: freedom of speech and freedom of religion
cards.hint: Also accepted: expression; assembly; petition; the right to bear arms

cards.front: What do we show loyalty to when we say the Pledge of Allegiance?
cards.hint: Also accepted: the flag

cards.front: What is one promise you make when you become a United States citizen?
cards.back: obey the laws of the United States
cards.hint: Also accepted: give up loyalty to other countries; defend the Constitution; serve if needed; be loyal

cards.front: How old do citizens have to be to vote for President?
What are two ways that Americans can participate in their democracy?
cards.hint: Also accepted: join a party or civic group; help a campaign; contact officials; write a newspaper

cards.front: When is the last day you can send in federal income tax forms?
When must all men register for the Selective Service?
cards.hint: Also accepted: between 18 and 26

decks.name: Colonial America and Independence
decks.description: Colonies, the Revolution, and the Founders (questions 58–70).

cards.front: What is one reason colonists came to America?
cards.hint: Also accepted: political liberty; religious freedom; economic opportunity; escape persecution

cards.front: Who lived in America before the Europeans arrived?
cards.hint: Also accepted: American Indians

cards.front: What group of people was taken to America and sold as slaves?
cards.hint: Also accepted: people from Africa

cards.front: Why did the colonists fight the British?
cards.hint: Also accepted: quartering of troops; no self-government

cards.front: Who wrote the Declaration of Independence?
When was the Declaration of Independence adopted?
Name three of the 13 original states.
cards.hint: Any three of the original thirteen are accepted

cards.front: What happened at the Constitutional Convention?
cards.hint: Also accepted: the Founding Fathers wrote the Constitution

cards.front: When was the Constitution written?
Name one writer of the Federalist Papers.
cards.hint: Also accepted: Alexander Hamilton; John Jay; Publius

cards.front: What is one thing Benjamin Franklin is famous for?
cards.hint: Also accepted: oldest member of the Constitutional Convention; first Postmaster General; Poor Richard’s Almanac; free libraries

cards.front: Who is the “Father of Our Country”?
Who was the first President?
What territory did the United States buy from France in 1803?
cards.hint: Also accepted: Louisiana

cards.front: Name one war fought by the United States in the 1800s.
cards.hint: Also accepted: War of 1812; Mexican-American War; Spanish-American War

cards.front: Name the U.S. war between the North and the South.
cards.hint: Also accepted: the War between the States

cards.front: Name one problem that led to the Civil War.
cards.hint: Also accepted: economic reasons; states’ rights

cards.front: What was one important thing that Abraham Lincoln did?
cards.hint: Also accepted: saved the Union; led the United States during the Civil War

cards.front: What did the Emancipation Proclamation do?
cards.hint: Also accepted: freed slaves in the Confederacy / most Southern states

cards.front: What did Susan B. Anthony do?
cards.hint: Also accepted: fought for civil rights

cards.front: Name one war fought by the United States in the 1900s.
cards.hint: Also accepted: World War I; Korean War; Vietnam War; Persian Gulf War

cards.front: Who was President during World War I?
Who was President during the Great Depression and World War II?
Who did the United States fight in World War II?
Before he was President, Eisenhower was a general. What war was he in?
During the Cold War, what was the main concern of the United States?
What movement tried to end racial discrimination?
What did Martin Luther King, Jr. do?
cards.hint: Also accepted: worked for equality for all Americans

cards.front: What major event happened on September 11, 2001, in the United States?
Name one American Indian tribe in the United States.
cards.hint: Many federally recognized tribes are accepted, including Navajo, Sioux, Apache, and others

decks.name: Symbols, Geography, and Holidays
decks.description: Rivers, territories, the flag, and national holidays (questions 88–100).

cards.front: Name one of the two longest rivers in the United States.
cards.hint: Also accepted: Missouri River

cards.front: What ocean is on the West Coast of the United States?
What ocean is on the East Coast of the United States?
Name one U.S. territory.
cards.hint: Also accepted: U.S. Virgin Islands; American Samoa; Northern Mariana Islands; Guam

cards.front: Name one state that borders Canada.
cards.hint: Also accepted: New Hampshire, Vermont, New York, and several others

cards.front: Name one state that borders Mexico.
cards.hint: Also accepted: California; Arizona; New Mexico

cards.front: What is the capital of the United States?
Where is the Statue of Liberty?
cards.hint: Also accepted: Liberty Island; New Jersey; Hudson River

cards.front: Why does the flag have 13 stripes?
Why does the flag have 50 stars?
cards.back: because there is one star for each state

cards.front: What is the name of the national anthem?
When do we celebrate Independence Day?
Name two national U.S. holidays.
cards.hint: Many pairs are accepted, including New Year’s Day, Memorial Day, and Christmas
